links.note: Five notes asked; two of them (Mazzini, Cavour) are the Italian unification figures and the stored answer develops Mazzini at length - Genoa, Carbonari, Young Italy, Young Europe. 23848 names Mazzini and Cavour explicitly. The other three parts reach 23845 (Greek war), 23846 (Frankfurt Parliament) and 23849/23846 (women).

Asks the steps taken to create collective identity, and the answer lists la patrie and le citoyen, the tricolour, the National Assembly, hymns and martyrs, centralised administration, uniform laws - 23842's description item for item.

Marianne and Germania as female allegories of the nation is 23849. 23850 is the sibling holding what the individual attributes (oak leaf, broken chains, crown) mean; this item asks who the figures were and why they were portrayed so.
Traces German unification - Prussia's wars and the 1871 proclamation. 23847.

Napoleon's administrative reforms in the territories he ruled: a centralised, rational administration and uniform law. FRAME GAP: this chapter's 12 concepts have no concept for section 1.2, Napoleon and the Napoleonic Code. 23842 is the only one whose description covers centralised administration and uniform laws, which is exactly what the answer describes Napoleon exporting.

Glossary item for 'plebiscite' - a direct vote by which all the citizens of a region accept or reject a proposal. Conceptually it is the instrument by which sovereignty sits with the citizens rather than a ruler, which is 23841. The three wrong options each restrict the franchise, so the discrimination is about who counts as the sovereign body.

Renan's argument that nations are a necessity belongs with the liberal case for nationhood (23844: government by consent, liberty, equality before law). DEFECT: the key is marked 'it ensures jobs and good health to all its inhabitants'. Renan wrote that the existence of nations is a guarantee of LIBERTY, which would be lost if the world had only one law and one master - option B. The key is wrong.

The French Revolution as the first revolution to give a clear idea of nationalism, with liberty, equality and fraternity - 23841, sovereignty passing to a body of French citizens who constituted the nation.

The first keyed statement is 23841's description verbatim: it is the people who would henceforth constitute the nation and shape its destiny. The other keyed statement (centralised administration with uniform laws) is 23842, but statement (i) is the primary one and the two false options are both about monarchy and custom duties.

The declaration that the French nation's mission was to liberate the peoples of Europe from despotism is a claim about what the nation is and is for, i.e. the idea of the nation, 23841 - not an administrative measure (23842).
The Civil Code of 1804 as the Napoleonic Code. Same frame gap as qid:87380: no Napoleon concept exists, and uniform law is 23842's content.
The Napoleonic Code being exported to the regions under French control - the spread of uniform law, 23842, under the same frame gap.
Liberal nationalism standing for freedom of the individual and equality before the law is 23844's description; the distractors are the conservative position (23845) and restricted franchises.
Universal suffrage as the right to vote for all adults, against the property-owning-men and men-only franchises. That contrast is made inside the liberalism section, 23844.

The false statement is that conservatives wanted a return to pre-revolutionary society and opposed modernisation; the text says most did NOT, and saw modernisation as strengthening monarchy. Conservatism is defined in the new-conservatism-after-1815 passage that 23845 heads.

The Greek war of independence and its settlement is one of the revolts against the post-1815 conservative order, 23845. DEFECT: no option is marked correct on this row at all - the answer is the Treaty of Constantinople 1832, which the duplicate of this item (qid:105348, filed under chapter 23710) does key correctly.

Poland partitioned at the end of the eighteenth century by Russia, Prussia and Austria is the pre-nationalist Europe of empires dividing peoples, 23843. 23845 would fit the 1831 Polish revolt, which this stem does not ask about.

Britain's nation-state emerging from Parliament's bloodless seizure of power rather than a sudden upheaval. FRAME GAP: section 4.3, the strange case of Britain, has no concept; 23843 is the nearest, since Britain's formation is the case of a kingdom assembling diverse ethnic peoples.
La patrie and le citoyen emphasising a united community with equal rights under a constitution is the first item in 23842's list of revolutionary measures.
Hymns composed, oaths taken, martyrs commemorated and internal customs duties abolished - all from 23842's list of measures taken in the name of the nation.
A centralised administrative system is named in 23842's description; the distractors are federal, regional and decentralised alternatives.

The Jacobin clubs' purpose - holding activities and campaigns that carried the idea of the nation outward. Grouped on 23841 with qid:106132 and qid:106134, the three items about exporting the idea of the nation.
The Jacobin clubs' campaigns preparing the way for the French armies to move into Holland, Belgium, Switzerland and Italy - the spread of the idea of the nation, 23841.
Nationalism as the idea the French armies carried abroad through the revolutionary wars - 23841 directly.
Napoleon introducing reforms in the territory under his control; the reforms in question are administrative and legal. Same frame gap as qid:87380.
Napoleon incorporating revolutionary principles in the administrative field to make the system rational and efficient - centralised administration, 23842, under the Napoleon frame gap.
The Civil Code of 1804 also known as the Napoleonic Code; duplicate of qid:106103. Same concept and same frame gap.

What the Civil Code brought about - privileges by birth abolished, equality before law, right to property secured. This is uniform law, 23842's content. 23844 also speaks of equality before law but as the later middle-class demand, not as Napoleon's statute.
The Code exported to the Dutch Republic, Switzerland, Italy and Germany - the spread of uniform law, 23842, under the Napoleon frame gap.

Napoleon simplifying administrative divisions, abolishing the feudal system and freeing peasants from serfdom and manorial dues in the countryside - administrative uniformity, 23842, under the Napoleon frame gap.

Guild restrictions removed, transport and communication improved, new freedom for peasants, artisans, workers and businessmen in the towns - the urban half of Napoleon's reforms, 23842, under the same frame gap.
Liberalism from liber, meaning free - freedom for the individual and equality of all before the law. 23844's description word for word.
